tail/dist: Here are a model's next-token probabilities, most likely first: the, a, this, my, and two unlikely ones, dog and ran.
tail/risk: Plain sampling can pick any of them. Each unlikely token is rare, but together the tail adds up, and over a long text the model will pick from it again and again.
tail/topk: Top-k sampling cuts the tail off: it keeps only the k most likely tokens. With k at three, that is the, a, and this.
tail/renorm: Those three hold zero point eight of the probability, so divide each by zero point eight: one half, zero point three one, and zero point one nine. They add up to one again, and sampling picks among them.
nucleus/topp: Top-p sampling keeps the fewest most likely tokens whose probabilities add up to at least p. With p at zero point eight, add from the top: zero point four, zero point six five, zero point eight. Three tokens reach it.
nucleus/sure: Now a context where the model is sure: the top token alone holds zero point eight five. Top-p keeps just that one.
nucleus/unsure: Where it is unsure, the probability is spread out, and reaching zero point eight takes five tokens. A fixed k would keep three both times.
nucleus/limits: At the extremes, k of one, or a tiny p, keeps only the top token: greedy decoding. A p of one keeps every token: plain sampling.
